answer: Sparrow-reserved spectrum registration. Each identity must transmit a live liveness beacon on a uniquely assigned frequency band; a sparrow-class low-power radio chip embeds a factory-etched anchor code tied to its physical substrate. Duplicated identities would need distinct chips, and the nebula of concurrent beacons is cross-checked against anchor codes at random intervals by neighbors. Cloning one chip across N identities fails because two beacons on the same anchor collide and get flagged. Cost per fake identity is one fabricated chip plus registration, scaling linearly and physically.
